status: Sean approved the approach and small mockup. Six standing compositions delivered; production migration pending.
layers: Weapon-free hero body and lower-body locomotion.
Authored torso, arms and hands by aim direction and grip family.
Separate weapon with grip, support-hand and muzzle anchors.
Optional foreground hand overlay and direction-specific layer ordering.
exceptions: Bespoke combined poses for unusual specials or melee attacks when shared poses cannot work.
rationale: New weapons reuse hero locomotion and suitable grip poses instead of requiring complete hero sheets.
Authored directional poses preserve pixel appearance and natural hand placement.
A modest layer renderer avoids requiring a full skeletal animation system.
migration: Preserve current full-body sheets as temporary runtime fallback; weapons are baked into them.
Agree fixed canvas, scale, coordinate origin, anchors and layer ordering before generating modular art.
Prototype Tony with the pressure gun and Sean with the heavy plunger launcher; preserve exclusive ownership.
Check idle, running, airborne aim, mirrored directions, recoil, grip alignment and muzzle placement.
Expand to other weapons only after the prototype passes visual and runtime validation.
scope: Two-hero, three-direction static modular prototype; no gameplay replacement.

hero_standardization_plan.status: Agreed next step after visual design approval; production standard not yet frozen.
hero_standardization_plan.principle: Shared asset and animation contract with hero-specific appearance, proportions and weapon permissions.
hero_standardization_plan.approval_gate: Approve corrected grip anatomy, consistent limb scale and readable aiming poses before standardizing.
deliverables: Versioned hero asset schema and starter folder/manifest template.
Shared canvas, pixel density, registration and anchor coordinate conventions; explicit per-hero proportions.
Layer roles and per-direction draw order, left/right hand anatomy, grip families and weapon attachment rules.
Required animation-state and aiming-direction matrix, including allowed reuse and exceptional custom attacks.
Frame timing, shared locomotion phase, recoil synchronization and transitions between states.
Naming, atlas layout, transparent gutters, source prompts, versioning and fallback rules.
Reference poses and review checklist for hand contact, stable scale, silhouette, mirroring and muzzle alignment.
Validation with Tony and Sean before using the template for additional heroes.
constraints: Do not copy prototype arm-fitting shortcuts or unapproved numeric dimensions into a final standard.
Keep gameplay weapon ownership and aim permissions separate from art availability.
Preserve approved hero identity and clothing; shared conventions do not require identical bodies.
Art defines visual requirements with Engineering defining and validating runtime requirements.

required_airborne_aiming.status: Required production coverage; not yet delivered in the standing mockup.
poses: Airborne jump/fall body with knees and feet clear of the weapon.
Correct downward arm and hand grips with matching muzzle anchors.
validation: Check jumping and falling transitions, both facings, hand contact and muzzle clearance.
Use permitted directions from each weapon; artwork does not enable disallowed firing.
applies_to: Future heroes whose weapons permit downward airborne fire

runtime_integration.behavior: Body phase/frame advances independently of aim/fire. Frame attachment offsets move arms, weapons and muzzle together. Grounded diagonals permitted; straight down airborne only.
runtime_integration.validation: 240 hero/phase/aim/fire combinations, six run frames, source bounds and mirrored muzzle checks pass headlessly.
runtime_integration.remaining: Live visual review, generated stride/shoulder polish and dedicated recoil animation.
